atomicity.reason: Two independent triggers (shutdown request and 60 s elapsed) are conjoined; each would stand alone as a complete requirement with different verification and different timing constraints.
atomicity.suggestion: Split into a shutdown-triggered write requirement (with its own completion deadline) and a periodic 60 s write requirement, sharing a separate record-layout requirement.

comprehensibility.reason: The record's three fields, the alternating two-slot scheme and both triggers are described inline, so the requirement reads on its own.

feasibility.reason: Feasible but pushes against non-volatile endurance: a 60 s cadence is roughly 30 writes per hour per slot, which over a vehicle service life lands in the 10^5 write range for each slot, close to typical EEPROM/emulated-EEPROM endurance.
feasibility.suggestion: Add an endurance budget or a change-gated write (skip the periodic write when the state of charge has not moved by more than a stated delta), and record the assumed memory endurance.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_SOC_STORE owns the two-slot alternating record - value, monotonic write counter and checksum - written on shutdown and every 60 s while awake; this requirement specifies that write.

unambiguity.reason: Two slot-selection rules are stated - 'the slot not used by the previous write' and 'always the one carrying the lower write counter' - which coincide only while both counters are consistent, and diverge after an interrupted or corrupted write.
unambiguity.suggestion: Make one rule normative (the lower write counter is the robust choice) and drop or derive the other, so the interrupted-write case has a single reading.

verifiability.reason: No deadline is given for completing the shutdown-triggered write and no tolerance for the 60 s period, so the shutdown case - the one that decides whether data survives - has no testable success condition.
verifiability.suggestion: State a completion deadline for the shutdown write (e.g. 'within 50 ms of the shutdown request, before the hold-up time expires') and a tolerance on the 60 s period.

summary: Weakest requirement alongside SWREQ_LIMIT_MINIMUM: two independent write triggers in one requirement, two slot-selection rules that can disagree after an interrupted write, no deadline for the shutdown write, and a 60 s cadence that stresses non-volatile endurance.
